name: Agent product positioning gaps
scope: Seed to Series A companies selling an AI agent as the primary product.

calibration.note: Axes 1, 2 and 8 are where most agent landing pages fail. If they do not dominate findings, treat that as a signal the rubric is miscalibrated, not that the company is fine.

axes.name: Unit of work
axes.buyerQuestion: What am I buying one of?
axes.dealStage: First call — buyer cannot price it, so cannot champion it internally.
probes: Does the page name a countable unit (per resolved ticket, per document, per hour saved, per seat)?
Is the unit the same one pricing is denominated in, or do the two disagree?
If the product is priced per seat but the value is per task, is that gap acknowledged anywhere?

axes.name: Failure behavior
axes.dealStage: Technical evaluation — the first hard question from the person who will own the incident.
probes: Does the page state what the agent does when it is uncertain or wrong?
Is there a stated accuracy, escalation path, or rollback story?
Are failures framed as handled, or is the page silent on the possibility?

axes.name: Blast radius
axes.buyerQuestion: What does it touch — auth, permissions, data?
axes.dealStage: Security review — stalls in procurement, often invisibly.
probes: Does the page enumerate what systems the agent reads from and writes to?
Are write actions distinguished from read actions?
Is permission scoping, data residency, or retention addressed?

axes.name: Human position
axes.buyerQuestion: Where am I in the loop, and can I get out?
axes.dealStage: Pilot design — determines whether the pilot is staffed or abandoned.
probes: Does the page say where a human approves, reviews, or intervenes?
Is the human-in-the-loop step presented as permanent or as training wheels that come off?
Is there a stated path from supervised to autonomous?

axes.name: Latency shape
axes.buyerQuestion: Real-time or async, and does that match my workflow?
axes.dealStage: Workflow fit — surfaces late, after the buyer has already imagined the wrong integration.
probes: Does the page say whether the agent responds in seconds, minutes, or overnight?
Is the interaction model (chat, queue, background job, webhook) stated?
Does the demo imply a latency the product does not actually deliver?

axes.name: Boring-case proof
axes.buyerQuestion: Does it work on the repeated case, not just the demo case?
axes.dealStage: Reference check — buyer asks an existing customer what it does on a normal Tuesday.
probes: Does the page show a high-frequency, unglamorous workflow?
Are the examples the hardest cases or the most common ones?
Is there volume or repetition evidence, as opposed to a single impressive anecdote?

axes.name: Refusal surface
axes.buyerQuestion: What does it explicitly not do?
axes.dealStage: Scoping — an unbounded product invites out-of-scope expectations that later read as failure.
probes: Does the page state anything the agent will not attempt?
Are limits framed as deliberate design, or absent entirely?
Does the breadth of claims make the product sound unbounded?

axes.name: Time-to-first-value
axes.buyerQuestion: How long until I see it work on my own data?
axes.dealStage: Top of funnel — determines whether the buyer starts at all.
probes: Does the page state how long setup or onboarding takes?
Can the buyer see it work on their own data without a sales call?
Is there a self-serve trial, sandbox, or sample run — and is the path to it stated?
